page: Microsoft Azure FX8-2mds_v2 is a specialized constrained-core virtual machine hosted on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, operating at a high clock speed of 4.2 GHz across 1 physical core and 2 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. The processor architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB shared L3 cache. Hardware-level acceleration is present for vector and matrix computations via AVX-512 and Intel AMX instruction sets.

The hardware configuration pairs 2 vCPUs with 168.0 GB of system memory, yielding an extreme memory density of 84.0 GB per vCPU. Direct-attached local storage is included via a 472 GB NVMe SSD. In benchmark testing, the 4.2 GHz clock frequency provides strong single-thread execution, reaching a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2344.0 and achieving 34.85 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. However, the physical limitation of a single dual-threaded core restricts parallel compute, resulting in bottom-quartile scores in multi-core Geekbench (2872.0) and stress-ng multi-core tests (2214.49), alongside an uncached large-block read memory bandwidth of 21.09 GB/sec.

Architecturally and economically, the FX8-2mds_v2 is suited for applications constrained by per-core software licensing where maximum memory capacity and high per-thread performance are necessary. The primary tradeoff is reduced overall aggregate throughput relative to standard multi-core nodes. This profile makes the instance effective for licensed relational database management systems, in-memory key-value caches, and memory-intensive single-threaded data transformation tasks requiring local NVMe scratch storage.
description: Microsoft Azure FX8-2mds_v2 is a memory-dense, constrained-core virtual machine powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Configured with 1 dedicated physical core delivering 2 vCPUs, it pairs an exceptional 168.0 GB of RAM (84.0 GB per vCPU) with 472 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 260 MB of L3 cache. Advanced instructions such as AVX-512 and AMX are supported. In benchmark evaluations, the elevated clock rate secures top-tier single-core performance, recording 2344.0 in Geekbench single-core testing and 34.85 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. However, the limited core count yields modest multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth. This hardware configuration is economically advantageous for software environments bound by per-core software licensing fees, making it well matched for in-memory databases, relational database engines, and cache-heavy processing pipelines needing high memory per thread.
